title: Gold lenders keep opening branches as collateral thins
dek: Bajaj Finance plans about 2,800 gold branches by March from 2,022 and L&T Finance about 800 by December from 502, even as Manappuram's loan-to-value rose to 65.6% from 57.3% and Fedbank's stage 2 rose to 3.6%.

read: Gold lending has become a branch race on falling collateral; Q3 will show whether the short-tenor strain at Bajaj and Fedbank cures or ends in auctions.
sources: Vantage analysis of Q1–Q2 FY27 earnings calls of Bajaj Finance, L&T Finance, Manappuram Finance, Fedbank Financial Services and Shriram Finance; credit-bureau data (industry estimate); Vantage sector intel, 21 Nov 2026
notes: Branch counts and targets are from Q2 FY27 calls (Bajaj Finance: 2,022 gold branches, close to 2,800 by FY27 end; L&T Finance: 330 to 502 in H1, about 800 by end-2026; Fedbank: 831), except Manappuram, whose figures (about 500 new branches planned in FY27; loan-to-value 65.6% from 57.3%) come from its Q1 FY27 call because its Q2 call was not on the desk. Bajaj's ₹1,601 cr is the rise in stage 2 and 3 loans in Q2, which management attributed mainly to short-tenor gold loans and called transient. Fedbank's stage 2 and GNPA are company-wide but its book is about 54% gold; management calls the rise technical, from the move to periodic interest payments. The NBFC gold-loan delinquency share (1–30 days past due) is an industry estimate based on credit-bureau data, not company data.
